body:
I would first like to respond to Lobsterboy. (Just because his post
appears first chronologically)

I am not and have never been associated with the Montana Freemen. BUT,
I have met them. I was on a federal transport jet with three of them,
several years back. (Only because our cases were being adjudicated at
around the same times.) The transport picked us up at a federal prison
in Springfield, Missouri and took us all back to Montana. The Freemen
went on to the Seatle-Tacoma holding facility. (A temporary stop) I
don't know where they went after that.

One of them appeared to be the leader. Another came across as a farmer
who had somehow been screwed over by the government and was really
pissed off about it. The third guy was a co-hort of the leader and had
an amazing ability to recall facts and figures. Things like obscure
laws from many years ago. The leader was very charismatic, intelligent,
and engaging. He had an amazing ability to convince people of whatever
the hell he was trying to convince them of. I couldn't quite figure out
what his goal was. But, in fairness to him and the others, he told me
that they had him and the other Freemen locked in isolation for their
entire stay at Springfield FCI. I can tell you from experience, too
much time in isolation will make anyone a bit disoriented. No human
being can survive too much time being isolated.

Next, I will respond to Starvin' Marvin.

I agree 100% that "The mass media are mostly under the control of large
organizations that are integrated into the system." Pretty much
everything is controlled by large organizations these days. The bombs
certainly caught the attention of everyone. There is no denying it. I
simply cannot condone sending bombs to college professors, though.
Perhaps a credit agency or cell phone executive, but not college
professors. (This is a joke, please do not send any bombs to anyone.)

I still maintain that there is strength in numbers. If we want to bring
about change, we all need to get on the same page. I suspect that if
things continue the way they are, you will see a bunch of milionares
and billionares enjoying life, while everyone else is either homeless,
or at least really pissed off that their lives are not going anywhere,
permanently.
